title: As a robotics engineer, I can bring up a new robot — drivers, configuration, first motion — in hours rather than weeks
As a robotics engineer, I can swap sensors and actuators behind stable hardware-abstraction interfaces without rewriting application code
As a robotics engineer, I can integrate cameras, lidars, IMUs, and GPS with ready-made drivers and standard message types
As a developer, I can pull reusable packages or modules from a registry or ecosystem for common hardware and behaviors
As a robotics engineer, I can simulate my robot and its environment with realistic physics and sensor models before touching hardware
As a robotics engineer, I can run the same robot code against simulation and the real robot without a rewrite
As a developer, I can generate synthetic training data and run reinforcement learning at scale in simulation
As an ops lead, I can monitor the health, location, and status of a whole robot fleet from one dashboard
As an ops lead, I can push configuration changes across many robots at once with per-group targeting
As an ops lead, I can get alerts on robot faults, battery, and connectivity so issues are caught before customers notice
As an ops lead, I can teleoperate a remote robot with live video and responsive control over real-world networks
As a robotics engineer, I can inspect live topics, logs, and state on a deployed robot remotely to debug issues
As an ops lead, I can route autonomy failures to a human intervention queue where an operator resolves and hands back control
As a developer, I can capture sensor and telemetry data on-robot and sync it to the cloud with bandwidth-aware policies
As a developer, I can query and export collected robot data through an API or SQL for offline analysis
As a developer, I can feed collected robot data into model training and deploy the improved model back to the fleet
As an ops lead, I can deploy software updates over-the-air to robots with staged rollouts and rollback
As a developer, I can run automated tests of robot software in CI, including simulation-based regression tests
As a robotics engineer, I can implement emergency-stop and safety-interlock patterns the platform documents and supports
As an ops lead, my robots keep operating and buffer data locally when cloud connectivity drops, then recover cleanly
As an ops lead, I can control with roles and permissions who is allowed to command, configure, or view each robot
As a developer, I can build against official, typed SDKs in multiple languages (Python, TypeScript, Go, C++) that cover the platform's full surface
As an AI-native user, I can have an AI agent authenticate with scoped credentials and command a real robot end-to-end through the platform's API or SDK
As an AI-native user, I can express a robot task in natural language and have the platform plan and execute it
As an AI-native user, I can integrate vision-language-action or robotics foundation models into my robot's autonomy stack through supported tooling
